Mario Party Recompiled's netplay server (alpha)
===============================================

The server lets friends play online without a VPN or anyone forwarding a port: only the server needs a port the
players can reach. It doesn't run the game and needs no ROM. It passes each player's buttons along, and every player
still runs the game on their own computer. It holds one party of 2 to 4 players. The first player to join it hosts
that party (as if they'd chosen Host a Party) and everyone after joins it.

Players need the same release of the game as the server: in the game, Online Play, Play on a Server, then the
server's address (a name like play.example.com or an IP address, with :port if it isn't 7845) and its password.

Running it
----------
On any 64-bit Linux (it's a single file with no libraries to install):

    ./netplay-server                       # UDP port 7845, no password
    ./netplay-server --port 7845 --password "our secret" --max-players 4

Open UDP port 7845 to the internet: in the VPS's firewall or security group (and ufw/firewalld if it runs one:
`sudo ufw allow 7845/udp`), or on a home server, forward UDP 7845 on the router to it. The password can come from the
MP_NETPLAY_SERVER_PASSWORD environment variable instead, so it doesn't show in the process list.

Run in a terminal, it takes the commands below typed into it. It logs who joins and leaves to its output.

As a service (starts on boot, restarts if it stops)
---------------------------------------------------

    sudo install -m 755 netplay-server /usr/local/bin/netplay-server
    sudo install -m 644 netplay-server.service /etc/systemd/system/netplay-server.service
    echo 'MP_NETPLAY_SERVER_PASSWORD=our secret' | sudo tee /etc/netplay-server.env   # optional
    sudo systemctl daemon-reload
    sudo systemctl enable --now netplay-server
    journalctl -u netplay-server -f          # its log

To change its port or player limit, edit ExecStart in the .service file (sudo systemctl edit --full netplay-server).

Admin commands
--------------
Type them into the server's terminal, or send them to a running server (a service too) from the same computer:

    netplay-server ctl players               # who's on, their number, ping, address
    sudo netplay-server ctl players          # the service's (it runs as its own user)

    players                 who is on the server
    kick <player> [why]     removes a player (their number from `players`, or their name); they can join again
    ban <player> [why]      removes a player and keeps their address (everyone on their network) out until the
                            server stops
    bans / unban <n|all>    the bans, and lifting them
    password <text>         joining needs this password from now on (players already in stay)
    password off            joining needs no password
    lock / unlock           stops / lets new players join (players already in can still reconnect)
    max <2-4>               the most players the party takes
    release                 stops holding the host's place (below): the next player to join hosts
    end                     removes everyone, ending the party
    stop                    stops the server

What the admin changes lasts until the server stops: its options (or the .service file) are what it starts with. A
server running with another --port is reached with `netplay-server --port <port> ctl ...`.

Who hosts
---------
The first player to join hosts. When the host leaves (Leave, or closing the game), the next player to join hosts. When
the host only drops out (the game restarting back into the lobby after "Back to lobby", the game crashing, or a
moment without a connection), the server holds the host's place for them for 45 seconds, so they come back as the host whatever order
everyone reconnects in; `release` lets someone else host at once. Removing the host (kick, ban) ends the party for
everyone, as the host leaving does, and the party can be picked up again with Resume Party.
